A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Articulate3D dataset and prediction framework, renamed from ArtMask3D to USDNet. Both main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and articulation experiments, ablations, MultiScan transfer results, annotation agreement and connectivity prediction results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds SceneFun3D evaluation, URDFormer adaptation results and simulated robotic manipulation outcomes.

M1.justification: USDNet matches ArtMask3D's Mask3D backbone, dense origin/axis predictions, query-based axis branch and auxiliary point-to-center branch. Comparing v1 Figure 4 with v2 Figure 3 establishes continuity; the expanded architecture and loss descriptions do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on SceneFun3D, image-based synthetic-to-real transfer using URDFormer, and simulated robotic drawer opening. These substantially extend the evaluated data and task requirements beyond v1's retained Articulate3D, MultiScan, connectivity and LLM insertion experiments.

E2.justification: v1's MultiScan experiment compares only ArtMask3D with and without Articulate3D pretraining. v2 Table 6 additionally compares USDNet against SoftGroup† and Mask3D† on MultiScan. The comparator set for the original Articulate3D experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include selecting and cropping three images per object, assuming known object poses and evaluating part-box AP50 for URDFormer, plus PPO training with 1024 environments for 30,000 iterations. The original 42-scene test split and 2 cm voxelization remain unchanged; newly specified articulation thresholds are additional disclosure.

E4.justification: v2 adds a zero-shot versus fine-tuned URDFormer study testing synthetic-to-real generalization, robotics case studies and train/test label-distribution analysis. The dense-axis/origin ablations, MultiScan pretraining analysis, annotation-agreement check and size/category failure analyses were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for model performance. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds SceneFun3D joint articulation scores of 30.5 for USDNet, 22.4 for Mask3D† and 12.8 for SoftGroup†. Table 8 reports URDFormer zero-shot/fine-tuned AP50 of 22.7/35.1 on MultiScan and 16.4/38.2 on Articulate3D; Section 10.2 adds 87% drawer-opening success. Original benchmark, ablation, pretraining and connectivity scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.2 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the auxiliary point-to-center loss and weighted joint training objective. Its cosine-based axis and origin-to-axis distance losses formalize the construction already described in v1. No new theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the headline contributions to synthetic-to-real adaptation, direct robotic policy training and greater asset diversity than synthetic datasets. The third contribution shifts from establishing a benchmark to demonstrating downstream utility. The dataset and dense-prediction contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets URDFormer fine-tuning as improved real-world adaptability and explains how its mesh-fitting and axis-alignment biases motivate bounding-box evaluation. It also omits v1 Section 5.1's explicit exclusion of movable parts without interactable descendants; this omission does not establish that those parts were newly evaluated. Existing size and faucet-failure interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies loss weights, articulation acceptance thresholds, GPT-4o-based class-mass estimates, URDFormer data preparation and robotics hardware/training settings. Most original model settings are retained or relocated, but v1's separate 640-epoch interactable-part training detail is omitted. The embedded project-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantial synthetic/generated-assets discussion, including ProcTHOR, HSSD-200, URDFormer and MeshArt, and expands Table 1 to compare diversity and simulation readiness. This strengthens positioning around real-world assets and the synthetic-to-real gap beyond v1's predominantly real-scene annotation comparisons.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten, USD background is condensed and partly moved to the appendix, and the method receives a dedicated USDNet section. Experiments and downstream applications are reorganized, with corresponding appendix restructuring. The title and model name also change.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially redesigned, the annotation and network diagrams are redrawn, and new comparison tables, annotation-tool screenshots, split-distribution plots and robotics illustrations are added. Existing LLM examples, dataset histograms, connectivity plots and error-analysis figures are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the dataset's central transfer and simulation utility. Beyond v1's MultiScan pretraining and LLM insertion, it adds synthetic-to-real adaptation, SceneFun3D validation and a trained drawer-opening policy, while documenting losses and evaluation thresholds more clearly. Omitted scope and training details are drawbacks, and uncertainty remains unreported, but the added direct validation provides a substantial net quality gain.
